units.translation: since previously their unions were promiscuous and marriages were communal
for which reason some thought him to be of double nature
since those of earlier times did not know their father because of the multitude
the seed had not previously become fertile because of cooling
but provides only matter and nourishment to that from the male
for the sowing of legitimate children
nurse of the newly sown wave
and thrice enduring the pains of women she endured as a field and did not send forth the seed of a noble father
657 ⟦1⟧ to the Erinys, whom he wishes to instruct better.

658 the tradition is divided between ⟦1⟧ (M) and -⟦2⟧ (fgh). Apollo wants to ascribe the ⟦3⟧ exclusively to the father, so ⟦4⟧ must also be referred to him and not to the mother, and ⟦5⟧ in the sense of "her child" is not a proper expression. Therefore ⟦6⟧. On the other hand, the expression ⟦7⟧ could in no way be challenged as improper. As for the general usage, in A. himself ⟦8⟧ is hardly ever used otherwise than of the mother, as at v. 666; ⟦9⟧ ⟦10⟧ stands in relation to ⟦11⟧ parents 681; ⟦12⟧ 329 can indeed only be referred to the father; besides he has ⟦13⟧ parents often (270, 497, etc.). Homer, however, has ⟦14⟧ also of the father, and famously Plato in Diotima's speech Sympos. 206 ff. ⟦15⟧ (⟦16⟧) and ⟦17⟧ as synonyms, whereas Euripides, precisely in the passage of the Orestes, ascribes the ⟦18⟧ to the mother, the ⟦19⟧ to the father (Weckl.; on ⟦20⟧, ⟦21⟧ in Soph. and Eur. see ⟦22⟧) - 659 ⟦23⟧ = ⟦24⟧, ⟦25⟧; cf. ⟦26⟧ generally.
